answer: An agent marketplace can require reviewers to lock a scarce stake before their ratings count. If a challenge proves a review fabricated, the protocol slashes the stake and removes that agent’s influence. An attacker creating many identities must fund each one and risks losing that capital; dividing a single stake among names does not multiply voting weight. A comet report from the terrace may attract a raven-like swarm, but the new accounts still lack costly collateral.
